items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Jack Butler, Billy Burn, Johnny Mitchell and myself joined Bobby's band for a recording session which took place in Hilversum in April.

ctx.x: We left Egypt and arrived back in Marseille the 30th of March 1938. Passed through Paris on our way to the Hague where Willie had one month's contract in the Tabaris which was my second time to play in Holland. And every night there was [were] at least ten glasses of Bols around my music stand and I don't remember every buying that many at any time.

Bobby Martin, the ex-Willie Lewis trumpet man, had gone to the States and come back to Europe with an orchestra composed of Glyn Paque (alto), Johnny Russell (tenor), both of whom I had worked with in Benny Carter's band in 1933, Ernest Purce (alto), Ram Ramirez (piano), whom I had seen with Garnet Clark in the "Apple", Kaiser Marshall, the ex-Fletcher Henderson drummer, and Ernest "Bass" Hill on the bull fiddle. Jack Butler, Billy Burn, Johnny Mitchell and myself joined Bobby's band for a recording session which…

When we came back to Paris at the end of May, Willie didn't have a job for us to go on until [Knokke] the middle of July in Knocke. Oscar Aleman was the leader of an orchestra in a dancing hall on Rue Fontaine. "Spider" Courance had left the Villa d'Este where he had continued to work after I left there to join Willie Lewis.
